title: High-quality reference genome of Fasciola gigantica
author: Xier Luo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bxatpien

steps.title: Collect adult Fasciola gigantica
steps.instruction: Obtain one adult Fasciola gigantica from an infected buffalo in the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, following approval by the Guangxi University Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee.

steps.title: Generate PacBio long‑read data
steps.instruction: Extract high‑molecular‑weight DNA and sequence on a PacBio Sequel II system to produce 122.4 Gb of data (~88× genome coverage) with an average read length of 15.8 kb.

steps.title: Generate Illumina paired‑end reads
steps.instruction: Sequence the same DNA on an Illumina HiSeq PE150 platform to obtain 89.5 Gb (~66× coverage) of paired‑end reads for error correction.

steps.title: Generate Hi‑C chromatin‑capture data
steps.instruction: Prepare a Hi‑C library and sequence on an Illumina platform to generate 134 Gb (~100× coverage) of Hi‑C reads containing restriction‑enzyme site information.

steps.title: Assemble genome with Canu
steps.instruction: Assemble the PacBio reads using Canu v2.0, which employs an adaptive overlapping strategy based on tf‑idf weighted MinHash and a sparse assembly graph to avoid collapsing diverged repeats and haplotypes.

substeps.instruction: Run Canu v2.0 with default parameters on the PacBio dataset.
Remove haplotigs and overlapping contigs with Purge_Dups using read‑depth information.

steps.title: Polish assembly with Arrow and Pilon
steps.instruction: Improve the draft assembly first with Arrow (GenomicConsensus) using its hidden‑Markov‑model consensus model, then run Pilon three successive times with Illumina paired‑end alignments to increase local base accuracy.

substeps.instruction: Run Arrow on the Canu assembly.
Align Illumina PE reads to the Arrow‑polished assembly.
Execute Pilon polishing round 1, 2, and 3.

steps.title: Scaffold to chromosome level
steps.instruction: Use ALLHiC together with the Hi‑C paired‑end reads to construct chromosomal‑scale scaffolds, incorporating the putative restriction‑enzyme site information.

steps.title: Evaluate assembly quality
steps.instruction: Assess the assembly with three complementary methods: (1) run QUAST to align Illumina and PacBio raw reads and estimate coverage and mapping rate; (2) map Illumina PE reads with BWA, call SNPs with Samtools and Bcftools, and compute the predicted error rate as homozygous substitutions divided by genome length; (3) run BUSCO to estimate completeness of the gene set.

substeps.instruction: Execute QUAST on the final assembly.
Map Illumina reads using BWA, call variants with Samtools/Bcftools, calculate error rate.
Run BUSCO with the appropriate lineage dataset.

steps.title: Predict genes from RNA‑seq and homology
steps.instruction: Align RNA‑seq reads (SRR4449208) to the genome with HISAT2 v2.2.0, assemble transcripts with StringTie v2.1.3 and PASA v2.4, train Augustus v3.0.2 and SNAP v2006‑07‑28 on the repeat‑masked genome, perform homology searches of UniRef100 (75 612 plagiorchiida proteins) using TBLASTn (e‑value < 10⁻⁴) and refine structures with GeneWise v2.4.1, then combine all predictions with MAKER v3.1.2 to obtain a high‑confidence gene set.

substeps.instruction: HISAT2 alignment of RNA‑seq reads.
StringTie and PASA transcript assembly.
Train Augustus and SNAP on repeat‑masked genome.
TBLASTn of UniRef100 proteins (e‑value < 10⁻⁴).
GeneWise refinement of homologous hits.
Integrate de novo, homology, and transcript evidence with MAKER.

steps.title: Annotate gene functions
steps.instruction: Run InterProScan v5.45 to assign protein families, domains, functional sites and GO terms; BLASTp the predicted proteins against SwissProt and TrEMBL (e‑value < 10⁻⁴) and use the best hits for functional annotation; query KEGG orthology with BlastKOALA; finally perform GO/KEGG enrichment with clusterProfiler’s enricher function using all annotated genes as background.

steps.title: Identify repetitive elements
steps.instruction: Build a de novo repeat library with RepeatModeler v2.0.1, then run RepeatMasker v4.1.0 on the genome using the combined de novo library and the Repbase‑20181026 known repeat library.

steps.title: Analyze repeat distribution and age
steps.instruction: Use bedtools to intersect repeats with gene coordinates and classify them as intronic or intergenic; construct a repeat landscape by plotting Kimura divergence from RepeatMasker output; infer LINE insertion times by converting Kimura distance to age (t = d/2μ) with μ = 1.73 × 10⁻⁹ per base per year; calculate TE proportions in sliding windows of 50 (n = 50) and correct by the genome‑wide intron/intergene ratio.

substeps.instruction: bedtools intersect repeats and genes.
Classify repeats (intronic vs intergenic).
Plot Kimura divergence landscape.
Convert divergence to insertion age using μ = 1.73 × 10⁻⁹.
Compute TE proportion in sliding windows of 50.

steps.title: Build host‑parasite protein interaction network
steps.instruction: Download genome annotations for human, swamp buffalo, F. hepatica, F. buski, Clonorchis sinensis, Schistosoma mansoni and Taenia multiceps from NCBI/BIG; identify proteases and protease inhibitors in each dataset with BLASTp; obtain expression data from TISSUES and subcellular locations from UniProt; map F. gigantica secretome proteins to the human proteome using reciprocal best‑hit BLAST; retrieve STRING protein.links.v11.0, keep interactions with confidence ≥ 0.7, and visualize the final network in Cytoscape.

substeps.instruction: Download reference proteomes.
BLASTp to identify proteases/inhibitors.
Gather expression (TISSUES) and localization (UniProt) data.
Reciprocal best‑hit BLAST mapping of secretome to human.
Download STRING interactions, filter by confidence ≥ 0.7.
Plot network with Cytoscape.

steps.title: Perform gene family and evolution analysis
steps.instruction: Select the longest transcript per gene and discard genes with ORFs < 150 bp; cluster genes from the eight species with OrthoFinder v2.3.12 to define families (17 992 families); detect expansions/contractions with CAFE v5.0.0; align 559 single‑copy orthologs using MUSCLE v3.8.1551, trim alignments with Gblock 0.91b, infer a maximum‑likelihood tree with RAxML v8.2.12 (PROTGAMMALGF model), and estimate divergence times with PAML MCMCTREE running 2 000 000 MCMC iterations, sampling every 100 after a 1 000‑iteration burn‑in under an independent‑rates model (two independent runs for convergence); calibrate the tree using fossil ages for Animals (602–661 Ma) and the euarchontoglires‑laurasiatheria split (95.3–113 Ma).

substeps.instruction: Select longest transcript, filter ORF < 150 bp.
Run OrthoFinder v2.3.12 across eight species.
Run CAFE v5.0.0 for family expansion/contraction.
Align 559 single‑copy orthologs with MUSCLE.
Trim alignments with Gblock 0.91b.
Build ML tree with RAxML (PROTGAMMALGF).
Estimate divergence times with MCMCTREE (2 000 000 iterations, sample every 100, burn‑in 1 000).
Apply fossil calibrations (Animals 602–661 Ma; euarchontoglires‑laurasiatheria 95.3–113 Ma).
